transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I... I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me. It's usually the board members or my staff. I hear them right through the conference room walls, or even coming from my phone when it's completely powered off. They're always saying I'm ruining the company. It sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer them back before I even realize no one else in the room heard a thing. 

Which reminds me, I really need to get a new phone case. The one I have now is this awful shade of green. I bought it when I was on a business trip in Seattle last year. Have you ever been to Seattle? It rains so much there, but the coffee is just fantastic. I used to go to this little cafe near Pike Place Market every morning before my meetings. They had these amazing blueberry scones... anyway, what was I saying? Oh right, the phone. It's just a terrible color, and it doesn't even match my purse anymore.
Aside from these experiences, have you noticed any significant periods where your mood felt unusually high, energetic, or conversely, very low and hopeless?

High or low? No, I wouldn't say so. I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is just... regular, I guess. I have a normal amount of energy, but you kind of have to when you're running a company. 

I actually did switch to this new organic meal delivery service recently to help keep my energy steady in the afternoons. The packaging they use is completely biodegradable, which is fantastic because we're doing a massive sustainability push at work right now. I'm having my procurement team audit all our vendors. Our current paper supplier, his name is Gary, he is just impossible to negotiate with. And he always wears these awful, bright yellow ties. It's incredibly distracting. I really don't understand why people don't use a color wheel when they get dressed in the morning. I learned all about color theory in this elective I took back in college... art history, I think it was? The professor had this massive, bushy white mustache that bounced every time he talked. It looked exactly like a caterpillar just resting on his upper lip... I used to just stare at it the whole lecture... wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about?

Are these thoughts about the board members and staff conspiring against you the only thing that feels like it's not quite right, or are there other strange beliefs or ideas you hold that others might find difficult to understand?

No, it's just... it's just them. I don't have any other strange ideas. I just know what I hear them saying about me. It's so frustrating because I built this company from the ground up, you know? Back when we started, our first office was in this tiny strip mall next to a dry cleaner. The smell of those chemicals used to seep through the vents all day long. It was giving me these terrible migraines, so I had to go to this holistic acupuncturist on the weekends just to function. She used these tiny gold-plated needles... she said gold conducts energy better than stainless steel. I actually read an article about that in some magazine while I was getting a pedicure last month. The manicurist, she kept insisting I get this bright coral color, but I told her, coral is a spring color, and we are clearly in the middle of autumn. It's like people have no sense of seasonal appropriateness anymore. Just like my neighbor, he leaves his Christmas lights up until Easter... I mean, who does that? Oh, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me?
Since these experiences with the board members began, have you noticed any changes in your ability to perform your daily tasks, maintain your social relationships, or express your emotions?

Well, I... I suppose things have changed. I'm just not reliably able to run the division right now, or even keep up with basic executive decisions. It's embarrassing, honestly, but the senior staff have quietly taken over a lot of the work I used to handle myself. I just can't seem to focus on it. And at home, my husband has had to manage almost all the household responsibilities because I just leave things unfinished, or I don't start them at all. 

He's been doing all the grocery shopping, which is sweet of him, but he always buys the wrong brand of almond milk. I specifically told him to get the unsweetened vanilla one with the blue cap, but he keeps coming home with the original flavor that has the red cap. Red is such an aggressive color for a beverage container, don't you think? It reminds me of those old fire extinguishers we had in my elementary school. Our janitor, Mr. Henderson, he was terrified of fires. He used to do these surprise fire drills in the middle of winter, and we'd all have to stand out in the snow without our coats. I got frostnip on my pinky toe once because I was wearing these incredibly flimsy ballet flats. They were very fashionable at the time, but completely impractical for a Minnesota winter... wait, why was I talking about Mr. Henderson? Did you ask me about my husband?
How long have you been experiencing these auditory hallucinations and the feeling that your staff is conspiring against you?

I'd say it's been about the past three months. That's when I really started noticing the voices coming from the walls, or sometimes leaking out of my phone. I actually thought my phone was hacked at first, so I took it into the carrier store to get it completely wiped. The kid working there, he couldn't have been older than nineteen, and he had this massive silver ring on his thumb. It looked so heavy, I don't know how he even typed on the register. 

I used to wear a lot of chunky silver jewelry in my twenties. I bought this huge turquoise necklace at a flea market in Santa Fe. The desert air out there is just so dry, it completely ruins your cuticles. I had to buy this special jojoba oil just to keep my hands from cracking. Jojoba is such a funny word to say, isn't it? Ho-ho-ba. It sounds like a laugh. My uncle used to laugh exactly like that, this big booming belly laugh. He actually worked as a Santa Claus at the local mall one year, but he had to quit because the fake beard gave him a terrible rash. He tried using hydrocortisone, but... wait, I'm sorry. What were we talking about? Did you need me to check my phone?

I've noticed that while we talk, your mind often jumps to unrelated topics like your memories or your personal preferences; does this difficulty staying on track happen to you often in your daily life, or is it only happening here today?

Well, I... I guess it happens all the time now. It's not just here. It's like my brain just won't stay on the rails anymore. Even at the office, I'll be in the middle of a board meeting, trying to explain the quarterly projections, and suddenly I'm talking about the catering. Last week, they brought in these awful stale croissants for the morning meeting. I mean, if you're going to cater a breakfast, at least get a decent pastry, right? There's this little bakery down the street from my house, a French place, and they make the most incredible almond croissants. The baker, Pierre, he actually imports his butter directly from Normandy. He told me that American butter just doesn't have a high enough fat content for proper lamination. 

Lamination... that's such a weird word for baking. It makes me think of elementary school again, when the teachers would laminate our artwork so it wouldn't get ruined. I made this beautiful watercolor of a blue jay once, and my mother hung it on the refrigerator for years. The magnet she used was one of those cheap plastic ones shaped like a slice of pizza. It always annoyed me because the pepperoni circles weren't painted inside the lines. I hate when things are sloppy like that. It's just lazy manufacturing. I actually visited a manufacturing plant in China a few years ago for work, and the precision they had on the assembly line was... wait. Why did I bring up China? What did you ask me about my mind?
Have you found that you have less interest in the activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, or do you feel like you have less emotional range than you did before these experiences started?

I... yes, I think that's true. I used to be the person driving every idea, you know? I'd be calling people after openings, just full of energy about the work. I really did love it. But now... now I can just sit at my desk for hours, just staring at the agenda. I barely even speak to my husband or my staff anymore, and I just feel almost nothing about it all. 

It's strange, sitting at a desk for that long. My desk is mahogany. It's a beautiful piece of furniture, really. I bought it at an antique auction in upstate New York. The auctioneer had this incredibly fast way of talking, it was like he didn't even need to breathe. I always wonder how people learn to talk like that. Do they practice in front of a mirror? My daughter used to practice her lines for the school play in front of the bathroom mirror. She was a tree in the second grade. Just a tree. She had to stand there with her arms up like branches for twenty minutes. We made her costume out of brown felt and construction paper leaves. 

Felt is such a strange fabric, isn't it? It doesn't fray when you cut it. I used to make these little felt finger puppets when I was a kid. I made a whole family of mice once, and I kept them in a shoebox. The shoebox was from a pair of Keds. I lived in Keds when I was younger. Classic white ones. But you had to keep them clean, which was impossible if you played outside. My mother used to scrub them with an old toothbrush and baking soda. Baking soda is amazing, really. You can use it for baking, for cleaning, for... wait. Why was I talking about baking soda? Did you ask me about my desk?
